blocks.text: Dork grabbed for the firing switch.
Seth hooked both brown gloves beneath the damaged rim. His boots scraped outward until they held.
He pulled.
The crooked mounting split with a sound that carried across the square. A cable stretched between the rising turret and the hull. Its plug tore free.
Dork pressed the switch.
Nothing happened.
Seth lifted the whole turret clear.
blocks.alt: Zerdo tears the complete turret from the tank, its copper-ringed ray still mounted inside and its firing cable disconnected; Dork remains in the lower hull’s driver opening.

blocks.text: For a moment he stood beneath it, arms locked, looking up at all that steel. He could feel the weight through his shoulders. He could hold it.
Jenny was already moving.
“Keep it that side!”
Seth carried the assembly away from the driver's opening. Jenny reached the hatch before Dork could pull it shut.
He ducked toward the steering controls. She caught his wrist.
“Out.”
“This is Army property!”
“They'll want to talk to you too.”
She drew him up through the forward hatch. His shoes found the sloping armor, then the pavement. Billy came around the planter with two officers.
blocks.alt: Jenny brings Dork out through the tank’s lower forward driver hatch to waiting officers and Billy while Zerdo holds the detached turret safely to one side.

blocks.text: Dork twisted toward the tank. The first officer took his other arm.
“You saw who broke it!”
Billy looked at the two tiny police cars beside the curb.
“We saw quite a bit.”
He led the officers back behind the stone corner. Dork went with them, still talking.
Seth lowered the turret onto clear pavement. He turned its copper opening toward the empty stretch of road and kept both hands against the shell while Jenny crouched beside it.
Through the torn underside she could see the gray box. Two steel straps held it against the front plate. The broken control cable hung loose beneath it.
A firefighter brought a socket wrench from his truck. Jenny fitted it over the first exposed nut.
“Hold this steady.”
“I am.”
“I meant the strap.”
Seth shifted one hand.
She loosened both straps, unplugged the remaining short lead and slid the box backward. The copper rings came through the front plate with it.
blocks.alt: Jenny uses a socket wrench to release the ray’s mounting straps inside the detached turret as Zerdo steadies it; the intact gray box and copper emitter come out together.

blocks.text: Seth took its weight until she had a proper grip. Then Jenny carried the disconnected ray around the corner to Billy and the officers.
When she came back, the firefighter had moved his truck. The street ahead was empty.
Jenny switched off the engine and checked the driver's compartment, then the open space beneath the missing turret. She pulled out the ignition key and held it up.
“Nobody left.”
Billy called from behind the corner. “We're clear!”
Seth picked up the empty turret shell.
Jenny stepped back beside the planter.
He swung.
The turret came down across the empty hull.
blocks.alt: Zerdo brings the empty turret shell down onto the evacuated tank, crushing its armor and buckling its tracks; Terminal Tower stands intact beyond the cleared street.

blocks.text: Armor folded inward. A track jumped from its wheels and struck the pavement in a long iron loop. The other side buckled beneath the blow.
The tank settled with a grinding crash.
Dust rolled across Seth's boots. He let the ruined shell rest in the hollow it had made and stepped away.
Above the square, Terminal Tower stood untouched.
A sharp clang came from the rooftops.
Seth looked up.
One fight was still going.
Fist dropped toward the wreck. Jaws followed, iron teeth snapping behind the white panel on his cuff.
“Running out of city, glove?”
Fist stopped above the open driver hatch.
Jaws lunged.
The glove slipped sideways. Metal teeth struck the thick edge of the hatch instead. Jaws scraped a bright groove into it and pulled back, furious.
Fist hit him from below.
The jaws clanged shut. Before they could open again, Seth caught the metal casing between his gloves.
Jaws jerked upward. Seth held him low over the empty armor, fingers clear of the teeth.
“Jenny. That bent strap.”
One of the ray's heavy mounting straps lay beside the detached cable. Jenny brought it over.
Seth bent the steel around the outside of the iron jaw. He folded its ends together beneath the casing, holding the upper and lower metal sections closed. Nothing covered Jaws's nose or eyes.
blocks.alt: With Fist hovering beside him, Zerdo folds a heavy steel mounting strap around Jaws’s closed metal jaw casing; the bodyless head’s nose and eyes remain clear.

blocks.text: Jaws tried to bite. His teeth could not part far enough to catch the strap.
He flew toward the street. Seth caught the brace and brought him back.
“Still flies,” Fist said.
“Then I'm not letting go.”
Fist hovered beside the captive head. The red leather around his own cuff was whole.
“That's enough biting.”
Jaws glared at him. There was still no recognition in his eyes.
Jenny returned to the police car.
Laura had not got inside. She stood beside the open door, watching the wreck over the officer's shoulder. Water dripped from her ponytail.
The extinguisher officer stayed back as a fire crew brought a charged hose around the corner.
Laura looked at the nozzle, then at Jenny.
“I'm not going back in that water.”
“Then don't fire.”
A small bright bead formed at Laura's lips. Jenny shifted at once, drawing her aim toward the empty stone wall. The firefighter raised his hose.
Laura closed her mouth. The light went out.
For a moment Jenny waited, feet apart, ready to move.
Then Laura lowered her eyes.
“I'm done.”
blocks.alt: The soaked, coatless Laura lowers her gaze and surrenders beside the police car; Jenny stays alert while officers and a firefighter with a charged hose maintain their distance.

blocks.text: Jenny stayed with the escort. She pointed out the scorched pavement and repeated her warning about Laura's mouth. An ordinary back seat would not hold Laura if she changed her mind.
He called for a different transport and a fire crew to accompany it.
Across the street, Seth held Jaws while Billy spoke into the police radio. Fist watched above them. Dork sat between two officers behind the corner, his hands cuffed.
The tank did not move again.
